name: Xârâcùù
catalog_citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Bulletin de la Société de Linguistique de Paris 73(1): 415-443.

catalog_quote: Toute unité non segmentable susceptible d'apparaître comme un élément libre dans l'énoncé est accentuable sur l'initiale. L'initiale accentuée est à la fois plus intense et plus haute que le segment non accentué qui la suit. L'accent porte sur la première more des unités brèves, ne comportant pas plus de trois mores, alors qu'il frappe les deux premières mores des unités qui en comptent quatre ou davantage. La more vaut une voyelle brève ou la moitié d'une voyelle longue et l'initiale accentuée de deux mores peut être de forme (C)V̄(C)V̄ ou (C)V̄. Il n'est pas certain que l'intensité soit également répartie sur ces deux mores initiales quelle que soit leur structure phonématique, en revanche elles contrastent régulièrement par leur hauteur avec les syllabes non accentuées suivantes. [...] On peut sans difficulté classer le xârâcùù parmi les langues à morphèmes accentogènes et à accent d…
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Xârâcùù (xara1244) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title, Lionnet's 2018 WCCFL 36 talk on downstep in Paicî and Xârâcùù, has no online handout; its published proceedings version (Lionnet 2019, already held by the project under paic1239) dropped Xârâcùù entirely. Its Xârâcùù content was published as Lionnet 2025 (Diachronica 42: 406-427; open author draft lingbuzz 008033 downloaded and read): every lexical word carries a predictable left-edge accent realized as a pitch drop after the first mora (words of 1-3 morae) or after the first bimoraic foot (4+ morae); the language is non-tonal and the accent is culminative, obligatory and demarcative — a description based on Rivierre 1978 (BSLP 73: 415-443, the sole primary phonological source, not obtainable online; high priority) plus Rivierre's 1977 Pangloss recordings. Three open first-hand Moyse-Faurie texts (1991 PL C-117 p. 306; 2004 HDR pp. 49, 87; 2015 valency chapter preprint p. 51) independently state initial-syllable accent/stress in Xârâcùù, with lower-register accents on dependents and second verbs in series (Rivierre's 'couplage'). Grace 1975 Canala dictionary (open, downloaded) is silent on stress. Unread: Moyse-Faurie 1995 grammar (HathiTrust search-only, could not be reached by automated download; Harvard print), Moyse-Faurie & Néchérö-Jorédié 1989 dictionary, and the 2002 Oceanic Languages sketch (print).

L'initiale accentuée est à la fois plus intense et plus haute que le segment non accentué qui la suit. [...] On peut sans difficulté classer le xârâcùù parmi les langues à morphèmes accentogènes et à accent démarcatif
new_statements.translation: Every non-segmentable unit that can appear as a free element in the utterance is accentable on its initial. The accented initial is both more intense and higher than the unaccented segment that follows it. The accent falls on the first mora of short units, those with no more than three morae, whereas it strikes the first two morae of units that have four or more. A mora equals a short vowel or half of a long vowel, and the accented two-mora initial may be of the shape (C)V(C)V or (C)V̄. [...] Xârâcùù can without difficulty be classed among languages with accent-bearing morphemes and demarcative accent.
new_statements.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Bulletin de la Société de Linguistique de Paris 73(1): 415-443.
new_statements.locator: §1.1 'Faits accentuels', p. 417 (PDF p. 3 of the extracted article; PDF p. 467 of the archive.org volume)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (29 pp. = BSLP 73(1) pp. 415-443; Rendered PDF p. 3 (= printed p. 417) with page render and read the page image: the passage under 'Faits accentuels / 1.1.' reads exactly as quoted — 'Toute unité non segmentable susceptible d'apparaître comme un élément libre dans l'énoncé est accentuable sur l'initiale. L'initiale accentuée est à la fois plus intense et plus haute que le segment non accentué qui la suit. L'accent porte sur la première more des unités brèves, ne comportant pas plus de trois mores, alors qu'il frappe les deux premières mores des unités qui en comptent quatre ou davantage. La more vaut une voyelle brève ou la moitié d'une voyelle longue et l'initiale accentuée de deux…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level accent (pitch + intensity, not tone) is fixed on the left edge of every free morpheme/word: on the first mora in words of 1-3 morae, and spread over the first two morae (the first bimoraic foot) in words of 4+ morae; it is culminative, obligatory, demarcative and fully predictable (Lionnet 2025 reanalyses it as a downstep after the initial mora/foot). Lynch 2002 (from Moyse-Faurie 1995) restates it in syllables: initial syllable in 1-3-syllable words, first two syllables in longer words.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary stress reported. Within phrases ('couplage', Rivierre 1978 pp. 418-425) the recessive unit keeps its initial accent but at a lower register, giving a stepwise falling melody; Moyse-Faurie 1991:306 / 2004:87 describe verb series as 'main accent on the first syllable of the first verb, with an accent on a lower register on the first syllable of the second verb'.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent contrast weakens as units get shorter; the accent of monomoraic units is often only virtual in connected speech (p. 417). Suffixed enclitic pronouns are wholly unaccented (fn. 3 p. 419). Under coupling, bimoraic words optionally lose or displace their accent (Lionnet 2025 §3.2), while 4+-mora words keep it in all positions. Articles a/ni and some prepositions are 'disjoint' (uncoupled).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'unité non segmentable susceptible d'apparaître comme un élément libre' = free morpheme/word, with examples in isolation (körôpaa 'canoe', kamûrû 'person'); coupling then organises words into accentual phrases by register. Compounds form a single phonological word accented on the initial (Rivierre p. 424; Moyse-Faurie 2015:51). Based on ten sessions with one speaker (Guy Tamai, Thio region), October 1977; not instrumental.
new_statements.identity_note: Rivierre 1978 describes 'la langue de Canala (xârâcùù)' from one speaker from the Thio region (Guy Tamai), i.e. the Thio-Canala variety = xara1244; Lynch 2002 / Moyse-Faurie 1995 cover the same Thio-Canala language. Some dialect differentiation exists (Moyse-Faurie & Néchérö-Jorédié 1989:15-18) but no separate Glottolog codes. Rivierre notes the sister language Xârâgurè (xara1243) has an accent system 'assez proche', but that is not described. The archive.org scanned renders the language name as 'zäräcii/æärâcii'; the page image reads xârâcùù.

new_statements.quote: Every lexical word in Xârâcùù is marked by a pitch drop at the left edge of the word. This pitch drop occurs after the first mora in words of less than four morae, after the second mora in words of four morae and above. [...] The accentual pitch drop satisfies all three of the accent-defining criteria discussed in §2.4 above. As shown by Rivierre (1978), it is culminative (there may only be one per word) and obligatory (every lexical word has one [...]). It is also demarcative, as it highlights the left edge of the word – specifically the initial mora or foot. It is thus unambiguously accentual. It is also fully predictable.
new_statements.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2025. Accent and tone: The double origin of the Paicî prosodic system. Diachronica 42(3-4): 406-427. doi:10.1075/dia.24039.lio. Author draft lingbuzz/008033 (the version read), Section 3.1 'Metrical conditioning of the Xârâcùù accent'.
new_statements.locator: §3.1, draft p. 9 (pdf p. 9); examples (14)-(16); accent-defining criteria same page; §3 intro p. 8 states the description is based mostly on Rivierre 1978 plus Rivierre & Tamai's 1977 recordings
new_statements.reading: Fixed, predictable, left-edge word accent (non-tonal language): the accent is a pitch drop (downstep) after the first mora in words of 1-3 morae and after the first bimoraic foot (second mora) in words of 4+ morae — i.e. word-initial accent with a mora/foot-conditioned realization site; one accent per lexical word. Independently corroborated first-hand by Moyse-Faurie (2004 HDR p. 49: 'chacun étant accentué sur l'initiale'; 2015: compounds 'stressed on the first syllable'; 1991 p. 306: main accent on the first syllable of the first verb). The primary description remains Rivierre 1978 (BSLP 73: 415-443), not obtained.

sources.note: Xârâcùù is non-tonal with a culminative, obligatory, demarcative, fully predictable word accent realized as a pitch drop (downstep) at the LEFT edge of every lexical word: after the first mora in 1-3-mora words, after the second mora (i.e. after the first bimoraic foot, within a colon) in words of 4+ morae. Under 'coupling' (Rivierre 1978) dependents are integrated into the head's register span and keep their accent at a lower register. Lionnet's description is 'based mostly on Rivierre's (1978) published article', supplemented by his own transcription of Rivierre & Tamai's 1977 Pangloss reco…

sources.note: The 2018 talk itself has no online handout (Glottolog record carries no URL; author's papers page lists only the published version). The published proceedings paper (Lionnet 2019, held by the project under paic1239, read in full) retitled the work 'Tonal evidence from Paicî' and does not mention Xârâcùù at all (a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits; abstract page confirms). Its Xârâcùù half — the accentual downstep = word accent — was written up in Lionnet 2025 (Diachronica), downloaded and read below. In Xârâcùù the 'downstep' IS the word-accent marker, so the talk is about accent…

sources.quote: p. 49: La succession Nom+verbe statif pourrait constituer un énoncé minimum, s'il ne s'en distinguait du point de vue accentuel. Ainsi, dans le cadre du syntagme, il se produit un "phénomène de couplage accentuel" (Rivierre, 1978), tandis que les mêmes termes en structure d'énoncé auront une accentuation disjointe, chacun étant accentué sur l'initiale, et à un même registre. — p. 87: Du point de vue accentuel, ils forment une entité au schéma bien particulier : on observe une chute accentuelle en cascade, l'accent principal portant sur la première syllabe du premier verbe, tandis que l'accent portant sur la première syllabe du deuxième verbe de la série se trouve à un registre inférieur à celui du premier verbe (cf. Rivierre). [EN: p. 49: The sequence Noun + stative verb could constitute a minimal utterance if it were not distinguished accentually: within the phrase an 'accentual coupling' occurs (Rivierre 1978), whereas the same words in utterance structure have disjoint accentuation, each accented on the initial (syllable) and at the same register. p. 87: Accentually they form a unit with a very particular pattern: a cascading accentual fall, the main accent on the first syllabl…
sources.locator: p. 49 (pdf p. 50), Xârâcùù noun + stative verb; p. 87 (pdf p. 88), Xârâcùù verb serialisation, fn. 25 citing Rivierre 1978 BSLP 73(1): 415-443
sources.note: p. 49: N + stative verb as a minimal sentence has 'une accentuation disjointe, chacun étant accentué sur l'initiale, et à un même registre', versus 'couplage accentuel' (Rivierre 1978) inside the NP; p. 87: verb series show 'une chute accentuelle en cascade, l'accent principal portant sur la première syllabe du premier verbe' with the second verb's initial accent at a lower register. Second-hand (cites Rivierre 1978).

sources.quote: Verb series make up an indivisible whole and contain no relational morphemes. They share a common case frame, common modifiers, and common tense-aspect markers. As a whole, they have a special falling accent pattern: the main accent falls on the first syllable of the first verb, with an accent on a lower register on the first syllable of the second verb.2 [fn. 2:] For a description of accent in Xaracuu, see Rivierre (1978).
